bodies.name: Ceres
bodies.notes: Orbit: JPL SBDB osculating heliocentric elements, epoch JD 2461200.5. Radius = JPL mean (volume-equivalent) radius; mass from JPL dwarf-planet table (Park et al. 2016, Nature 537:515, Dawn gravity). Ceres is triaxial ~482x482x446 km semi-axes (964.4x964.2x891.8 km extents in SBDB).

bodies.name: Pluto

moons.name: Charon
moons.notes: a/e/P/mass: Brozovic & Jacobson 2024 (AJ 167:256); a is Pluto-centric. Radius: Nimmo et al. 2017. JPL GM 106.1 km^3/s^2 gives the same mass.

moons.name: Styx
moons.notes: JPL mean equatorial elements (PLU060, a rounded to 100 km). Radius from JPL table (irregular body, approximate). Mass not determined (JPL lists n/a).

moons.name: Nix
moons.notes: JPL PLU060 mean elements; radius JPL; mass from JPL GM 0.0015+/-0.0005 km^3/s^2 (~33% uncertain). Highly elongated body.

moons.name: Kerberos
moons.notes: JPL PLU060 mean elements; radius JPL (approximate, bilobed body). Mass not determined (JPL lists n/a).

moons.name: Hydra
moons.notes: JPL PLU060 mean elements; radius JPL; mass from JPL GM 0.0020+/-0.0003 km^3/s^2. Elongated body.

bodies.notes: Orbit: JPL SBDB osculating heliocentric elements, epoch JD 2457588.5. SBDB's Pluto orbit solution has an older epoch (JD 2457588.5 = 2016-Jul-31) than the others. Radius 1188.3 km (Archinal et al. 2018 / New Horizons); mass 1.30246e22 kg (Brozovic & Jacobson 2024) from JPL dwarf-planet table. Moon a/P/e for small moons are JPL mean equatorial elements (Pluto-centric).

bodies.name: Haumea

moons.name: Hiʻiaka
moons.notes: Orbit: Ragozzine & Brown 2009 (AJ 137:4766). Radius = half of 370+/-20 km diameter and mass 1.6+/-0.2e19 kg from Fernandez-Valenzuela et al. 2025 (Nature Communications 16) stellar occultation.

moons.name: Namaka
moons.notes: Orbit: Ragozzine & Brown 2009; orbit is strongly perturbed (non-Keplerian) by Hi'iaka so e and a vary. Radius = half of 150+/-50 km diameter (Fernandez-Valenzuela et al. 2025, poorly constrained). Mass 1.18+/-0.25e18 kg from Proudfoot et al. 2024 (PSJ 5:69).

bodies.notes: Orbit: JPL SBDB osculating heliocentric elements, epoch JD 2461200.5. Haumea is a strongly triaxial ellipsoid. mean_radius_km is the volume-equivalent radius computed here from Ortiz et al. 2017 (Nature 550:219) semi-axes 1161 x 852 x 513 km: (1161*852*513)^(1/3) = 797.6 km. A 2026 occultation paper (Proudfoot et al., arXiv:2605.28636, PSJ) gives a smaller volume-equivalent diameter 1544 km (axes 2122x1688x1036 km diameters) -> radius ~772 km; not yet adopted here. JPL's table lists 715 km mean radius (Lockwood et al. 2014) which is an older estimate. Mass 3.952+/-0.011e21 kg from Proudfoot et al. 2024 (PSJ 5:69); this is essentially the system mass (moons are <0.5%). Haumea also has a ring (a ~2285 km, Ortiz et al. 2017).

bodies.name: Makemake

moons.name: S/2015 (136472) 1 (MK2)
moons.notes: Discovered 2015 by Parker et al. 2016 (ApJ 825:L9). Orbit not well determined: a preliminary orbit (a = 22250+/-780 km, P = 18.023+/-0.017 d, e ~ 0) exists only as an arXiv preprint (Bamberger 2025, arXiv:2509.05880), so left null. Radius 87.5 km = half of ~175 km diameter assuming 4% albedo (Parker et al. 2016); 175-250 km diameter for 2-4% albedo, so radius is model-dependent. Mass unknown.

bodies.notes: Orbit: JPL SBDB osculating heliocentric elements, epoch JD 2461200.5. Radius 715+/-7 km: Brown 2013 (ApJ 767:L7), from occultation-derived ellipse 1434 x 1420 km (JPL table lists 714 km mean). Mass left null: no peer-reviewed determination. Published estimates are 3.1e21 kg (Parker et al. 2018, DPS abstract, used in JPL table) and 2.69+/-0.20e21 kg (Bamberger 2025 arXiv preprint, based on the preliminary MK2 orbit).

bodies.name: Eris

moons.name: Dysnomia
moons.notes: Orbit: Holler et al. 2021 (Icarus 355:114130). Radius = half of 615 (+60/-50) km diameter and mass 8.2+/-5.7e19 kg from Brown & Butler 2023 (PSJ 4:193, ALMA); mass very uncertain.

bodies.notes: Orbit: JPL SBDB osculating heliocentric elements, epoch JD 2461200.5. Radius 1163+/-6 km from stellar occultation (Sicardy et al. 2011, Nature 478:493). Mass 1.638e22 kg = Eris alone (system mass 1.6466+/-0.0085e22 kg from Holler et al. 2021 minus Dysnomia per Brown & Butler 2023). JPL's table lists older values (radius 1200 km, mass 1.66e22 kg; Brown & Schaller 2007).

bodies.name: Gonggong

moons.name: Xiangliu
moons.notes: Orbit from Kiss et al. 2019 (Icarus 334:3). Two mirror solutions fit: prograde (given: a 24021+/-202 km, P 25.22073 d, e 0.2908) and retrograde (a 24274 km, P 25.22385 d, e 0.2828). Size not well determined: estimated 40-100 km diameter (Kiss et al. 2019) or <200 km (Arakawa et al. 2021), so radius null. Mass unknown.

bodies.notes: Orbit: JPL SBDB osculating heliocentric elements, epoch JD 2461200.5. Radius = half of 1230+/-50 km diameter; mass 1.75+/-0.07e21 kg is the system mass from Xiangliu's orbit (Kiss et al. 2019, Icarus 334:3).

bodies.name: Quaoar

moons.name: Weywot
moons.notes: Orbit and mass: Proudfoot et al. 2025 (PSJ, arXiv:2511.07351); mass 2.4 (+1.2/-1.1)e18 kg is poorly constrained. Size not well determined: 116-172 km diameter (Fernandez-Valenzuela et al. 2026), so radius null.

bodies.notes: Orbit: JPL SBDB osculating heliocentric elements, epoch JD 2461200.5. Radius = half of the 1097.6+/-2.2 km volume-equivalent diameter (Proudfoot et al. 2025, PSJ, arXiv:2511.07351; occultation-derived triaxial shape 1166.6 x 1110.6 x 1020.0 km). Older occultation value: 1110+/-5 km diameter (Braga-Ribas et al. 2013). Mass 1.212+/-0.005e21 kg = Quaoar alone (Proudfoot et al. 2025). Quaoar has rings; a second moon is suggested but unconfirmed, so known_moons = 1.

bodies.name: Orcus

moons.name: Vanth
moons.notes: Orbit: Grundy et al. 2019 (Icarus 334:62). Radius = half of 442.5+/-10.2 km occultation diameter (Sickafoose et al. 2019, Icarus 319:657). Mass 8.7+/-0.8e19 kg (Brown & Butler 2023, PSJ 4:193).

bodies.notes: Orbit: JPL SBDB osculating heliocentric elements, epoch JD 2461200.5. Radius = half of 910 (+50/-40) km diameter (Brown & Butler 2018, AJ 156:164). Mass 5.478e20 kg = Orcus alone (system 6.348+/-0.019e20 kg from Grundy et al. 2019 minus Vanth 8.7e19 kg).

bodies.name: Sedna
bodies.notes: Orbit: JPL SBDB osculating heliocentric elements, epoch JD 2461200.5. Size poorly constrained, so mean_radius_km is null: thermal diameter 906 (+314/-258) km (Lellouch et al. 2013, A&A 557:A60) vs an occultation chord implying diameter >~1025+/-135 km (Rommel et al. 2020). No moons known, so mass unknown. Note: osculating heliocentric a (~544 AU) and period (~12,700 yr) differ greatly from the barycentric values (~506 AU, ~11,400 yr) that are often quoted; for a game, barycentric values are more representative of the long-term orbit.

bodies.name: Vesta
bodies.notes: Orbit: JPL SBDB osculating heliocentric elements, epoch JD 2461200.5. Radius = half of 522.77 km mean diameter; mass from GM 17.2882844 km^3/s^2 (Park et al. 2025, Nature Astronomy, Dawn) via SBDB, G = 6.67430e-11. Triaxial: 569.24 x 554.48 x 452.66 km.

bodies.name: Pallas
bodies.notes: Orbit: JPL SBDB osculating heliocentric elements, epoch JD 2461200.5. Radius = half of 513 km diameter (Marsset et al. 2020, Nature Astronomy 4:569); mass from GM 13.63 km^3/s^2 (Vernazza et al. 2021, A&A 654:A56) via SBDB. Shape 568 x 532 x 448 km.

asteroid_belt.notes: Main-belt 'core' bounded by the 4:1 and 2:1 Kirkwood gaps (mean-motion resonances with Jupiter) at 2.06 and 3.27 AU (Wikipedia 'Asteroid belt', based on MPC orbit data). Check via Kepler's 3rd law: 5.2026*(1/4)^(2/3)=2.065 AU, 5.2026*(1/2)^(2/3)=3.277 AU. NASA describes the belt only as 'between Mars and Jupiter'. Popular sources also quote ~2.2-3.2 AU, but I did not find a primary source for that range.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asteroid_belt
https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/asteroids/facts/

kuiper_belt.notes: NASA: inner edge at Neptune's orbit (~30 AU); the inner, main region ends ~50 AU (Kuiper cliff). The classical (non-resonant) KBOs lie mainly between the 3:2 resonance at 39.5 AU and the 2:1 resonance at ~48 AU (de Sanctis et al. 2001, via Wikipedia); the cold classical population lies at 42-47 AU (Jewitt & Delsanti 2006, via Wikipedia).

notes: Orbital elements are JPL SBDB osculating heliocentric elements (epoch JD 2461200.5 = 2026-Jun-24 for all except Pluto, JD 2457588.5), rounded to 4 decimals (a, e) and 0.01 deg. longitude_of_perihelion_deg = (node + argument of perihelion) mod 360. orbital_period_years = SBDB period (days)/365.25. Osculating heliocentric values for distant TNOs differ slightly from barycentric ones (substantially for Sedna). Masses derived from GM use G = 6.67430e-11. Where a primary has a moon, the 'mass' of the primary is either primary-only (Eris, Quaoar, Orcus) or system (Haumea, Gonggong) as stated in each body's notes. Moon semi-major axes are relative to the primary (planetocentric). For TNO dwarf planets, size and mass values come from recent papers and carry real uncertainty; check each note. Null means no value could be verified from a peer-reviewed or JPL source.
